description: §40.8 / §6.7.4 (S432) — a bare `when @n changes { … }` at the `<program>` default-logic body-top, written AFTER the first markup child, is a registered reactive effect — not literal page text. Pre-fix it lifted only when it shared a text run with a preceding declaration; after markup (or a `${}` block, or a `//` comment) it shipped as page text at exit 0 with zero diagnostics.
rationale: §40.8: the `<program>` body parses in default-logic mode; the lifecycle statements `on mount {}` / `on dismount {}` / `when … changes {}` are lifted at its body-top like declarations, by their grammar head, wherever they sit among the body's children. §6.7.4: "A `when` statement declares a reactive effect. The body executes whenever any listed dependency changes value." Two #inc clicks drive @n 0 → 2; the effect runs exactly twice ("The body does NOT execute on initial mount" — @runs 2, not 3) and writes @doubled = 4; the statement's source never reaches the DOM.
